title: S3 Buckets & Objects Deep Dive 🪣
description: Understand the structure of S3 – buckets, objects, keys, prefixes, and performance considerations.

slides.title: Buckets: The Top‑Level Container 🪣
slides.content:
# Your Data's Home

Everything in S3 lives inside a **bucket**. Buckets are created within a specific AWS Region, but bucket names must be **globally unique** across all AWS accounts.

Naming rules:
- 3–63 characters long.
- Lowercase letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens.
- Must start and end with a letter or number.
- Must not look like an IP address (e.g., 192.168.5.4).

Once created, you can't rename a bucket. Delete and recreate if needed.

quizData.question: Which of the following is a valid S3 bucket name?
quizData.explanation: Bucket names must be all lowercase, cannot contain underscores, and cannot look like an IP address.

slides.title: Objects: Files + Metadata 📄
slides.content:
# The Basic Unit of Storage

An object consists of:
- **Key**: the full path within the bucket (e.g., `images/2025/photo.jpg`).
- **Value**: the data itself (up to 5 TB).
- **Version ID** (if versioning enabled).
- **Metadata**: key‑value pairs describing the object.
- **Sub‑resources**: Access Control Lists (ACLs), tags.

There's no true folder structure – the key simulates folders using `/` delimiters. S3 is a flat key‑value store; the console shows a folder tree for convenience.

slides.title: Key Naming Best Practices 🏷️
slides.content:
# Prefixes and Performance

Although S3 can handle massive request rates, using a **randomised prefix** at the start of keys improves performance for high request loads.

- Avoid sequential prefixes like `timestamp_0001`, `timestamp_0002`...
- Use a hashed or random prefix, e.g., `a7d2/`.

This is because S3 partitions keys lexicographically; a diverse prefix spreads load across partitions.

slides.title: Accessing Objects via S3 URI
slides.content:
Every object gets a unique URL:

`s3://bucket-name/key-name` (S3 URI) or `https://bucket-name.s3.region.amazonaws.com/key-name` (virtual hosted‑style URL).
slides.codeSnippet:
aws s3 ls s3://my-data-bucket/projects/2025/
# Upload a file
aws s3 cp report.pdf s3://my-data-bucket/reports/report.pdf

slides.title: Pro Tip: S3 Select 🚀
slides.content:
## Query Inside Objects

S3 Select lets you run SQL‑like queries on CSV, JSON, or Parquet objects and retrieve only the needed bytes. It drastically reduces data transfer and cost for analytics.
